title: AI and Digital Transformation
detail: Named in virtually every deep-dive interview as the most immediate skills gap; SMEs especially lack the capacity to assess and adopt AI safely and productively (LSIP p.23).

title: Net Zero and Green Skills
detail: Retrofit, low-carbon technologies and environmental compliance are needed across construction, manufacturing, clean energy and beyond, not as a standalone specialism (LSIP p.34,43).

title: Equality of Opportunity and Workforce Participation
detail: Economic inactivity in LCR is around 25% versus roughly 21% nationally; NEET young people and women in construction are priority groups for wider access (LSIP p.34-35).

title: Progression for the Existing Workforce
detail: Across every priority sector, technically competent staff are stuck below supervisory and specialist roles; Change 5 focuses funding on in-work progression, not just new entrants (LSIP p.40-41).

title: Work Readiness and Inclusive Pathways
detail: New entrants often hold qualifications but lack applied communication, literacy and workplace confidence; skills passports, digital badges and a literacy pilot aim to close this (LSIP p.42-43).

title: SME Access to Workforce Development
detail: Around 90% of the region's roughly 43,000 active enterprises are micro or small; time, cost and complexity keep them from training their staff (LSIP p.38).

title: The Local Triple Lock and Industry Skills Partnerships
detail: The LSIP works alongside the LCR Growth Plan and the Get LCR Working Plan, with new Industry Skills Partnerships (ISPs) giving employers a direct route to shape training (LSIP p.13-14,37).
